name: comp-46
title: Phone Number Input
description: A labelled phone field joined to a country selector. Typing an international number spaces the digits into a readable phone number and makes the selector detect the country and show its flag.
use: Sign-up or contact forms that accept phone numbers from more than one country.
avoid: It ships a visible third-party credit link and pulls in a sizeable phone-number library.
a11y: The label and country select are named properly, but a country detected from typing is not announced to screen readers. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A label sits above a joined control on black: a country selector holding a small handset icon and a chevron, then a long rounded input. Once a code is typed a US flag replaces the handset, and the digits run across in spaced groups.
behaves: Typing formats the number with spaces and the selector watches the country code, swapping in the matching flag. The clip enters +1 415 555 0132, the flag changes to the United States and the caret stays in the field.
customise: The label and placeholder are fixed in the file and the country list comes from the phone library; field and selector styling are classes there.
weight: moderate: Phone metadata plus parsing on each keystroke is heavier than a plain text field.
demo: Label Phone number, placeholder Enter phone number, typed +1 415 555 0132, plus a library credit line.
issues: A visible react-phone-number-input credit line ships under the field.
polishWhy: Tidy joined field with a nice flag reveal, though the credit line and plain styling hold it back.
